articles.title: Mountain Rescue Team Finds Missing 71-Year-Old Man Near Piethorne Reservoir
articles.excerpt: A 71-year-old man with dementia was found by a mountain rescue team near Piethorne Reservoir after being reported missing on Saturday. The search involved police and a helicopter.
articles.content_html:
A mountain rescue team successfully located a 71-year-old man with dementia who had been reported missing near Piethorne Reservoir in Newhey on Saturday evening. The search operation was initiated after Greater Manchester Police received a report regarding the missing individual, prompting a coordinated effort that included the use of a police helicopter.

The Oldham Mountain Rescue Team was called in to assist with the search. According to a statement from the team, the man was equipped with an air tag that indicated he was in the vicinity of the reservoir. Initial searches conducted by police and the helicopter did not yield any results, leading to the involvement of the mountain rescue team.

The rescue team mobilised to the dam wall at Piethorne Reservoir, where their water section began searching the edges of the water both on foot and using a raft. Meanwhile, two additional search sections covered paths and tracks that had not yet been searched by police. Search dogs were also deployed to aid in the effort.

The missing man was found by a search dog and its handler before they reached their designated area. He was reported to be cold and confused but was safely located and returned to safety. This incident highlights the importance of community and emergency services working together in search and rescue operations.

articles.title: Newhey Gardening Gang volunteers transform churchyard in latest community clean-up
articles.excerpt: Volunteers from Newhey's Gardening Gang have completed another major session in the local churchyard, cutting grass, tending shrub beds and cremation plots and clearing pathways.
articles.content_html:
A team of community volunteers has continued its work keeping a Newhey churchyard looking its best after another strong turnout for the local Gardening Gang.

Volunteers were back at work yesterday, tackling a substantial list of jobs across the churchyard and continuing the improvements made during previous sessions.

The group's 'buzzy bee strimmers' were out in force and completed the mammoth task of cutting all of the grass areas. Other volunteers weeded and cut back shrub beds and cremation plots, while a number of pathways were also cleared.

The work is part of an ongoing community effort to maintain and improve the churchyard, with local volunteers giving their own time to care for a space used by families, visitors and the wider Newhey community.

Organisers thanked everyone who took part, saying the churchyard continues to look great thanks to the efforts of the Gardening Gang.

Volunteer-led projects like this can make a significant difference to shared spaces, particularly where regular maintenance involves large areas of grass, established planting and paths which need repeated attention throughout the growing season.

The Gardening Gang is expected to announce another volunteering date, with residents being encouraged to watch for details of the next session.

Rochdale Daily would like to thank all of the volunteers giving their time to help look after Newhey's community spaces.

articles.title: Elderly lady found after incredible community effort
articles.excerpt: A woman in her 70s who went missing in Newhey has been found after hundreds of residents joined Greater Manchester Police in an extraordinary community search.
articles.content_html:
An elderly woman who went missing in Newhey has been found following an extraordinary community effort involving hundreds of local residents.

Christine, who is in her 70s, was reported missing earlier in the evening, prompting an urgent response from Greater Manchester Police and a huge mobilisation across Newhey and the surrounding area.

As concern grew, residents left their homes to help officers search on the ground. People walked streets, paths and open spaces, checked nearby areas and shared information rapidly across community groups in an effort to bring Christine home.

The response was remarkable. Hundreds of people are understood to have assisted either directly with searches or by sharing appeals and helping coordinate information alongside GMP.

At around 11pm, local woman Charlotte Rigby found Christine. In a touching detail after hours of worry, Christine was found clutching a bunch of flowers.

News that she had been located was met with enormous relief across the community, bringing a frightening evening to the best possible conclusion.

Tonight demonstrated Newhey and the wider Rochdale borough at its very best. Residents did not simply share a post and hope for good news. They put on their shoes, went outside and actively helped search for someone who needed them.

Credit must also go to Greater Manchester Police and everyone who supported the search, but special recognition is due to the countless members of the public who gave their time and refused to give up.

The borough should be very proud tonight. This was community spirit in its purest form, and the outcome is the great news everyone had been hoping for.

Out of respect for Christine and her family, no further personal or medical details should be shared unless released through official channels.
